transcript:
Header: 2026-04-01 10:00 AM UTC | Duration: 45m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Michael Grant (Astra Health CTO), Sara Lin (ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Platform)
Links shared: benchmark-spreadsheet.xlsx (drive link), redwood-security-whitepaper.pdf (link)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to go over this week's benchmark pass vs the baseline provider and call out the tuning we did, priya i'll hand it over to you for the numbers
[00:10] Priya: yeah hi, um so quick recap - we ran the 1k-sample prompt set from sara, same prompts you sent last week, token distribution roughly 40-120 tokens, mixture of generative and instruction. baseline provider we measured on their hosted endpoint, and we ran Redwood hosted plus a dedicated pool run.
[00:28] Priya: raw numbers first - baseline p50 120ms p95 420ms p99 820ms, throughput ~120 rps sustained on 8 concurrent workers, tokens/sec ~5k. Redwood hosted (default config) p50 95ms p95 320ms p99 650ms, throughput ~150 rps. Redwood dedicated (4x A100-ish like nodes) p50 70ms p95 240ms p99 480ms, throughput 210 rps.
[01:02] Michael: okay that's a pretty clear delta on p95, um can you confirm test harness was identical? like same batch sizes and prompt mixing?
[01:09] Priya: yes we used same harness but we had to tune batching on Redwood to match latency SLOs; baseline was using larger automatic batching which increased throughput but pushed p95 higher. also we enabled KV prefix caching for multi-turn prompts which dropped p50 on continuing conversations by about 30%.
[01:26] Tom: when you say kv cache, that's the session-level kv cache, right? is that supported on the baseline provider too?
[01:31] Priya: baseline has some caching but it's not integrated with their rerouting, and their cache TTLs are shorter; Redwood's KV cache kept hot prefixes for longer which helped our p50/p95 on follow-up prompts.
[01:43] Sara: curious about quantization - we saw you ran a 4-bit quantized variant in the sheet, what's the quality impact?
[01:48] Priya: good question - quantized mpt-7b-fast variant bumped throughput by ~25% and reduced p95 by ~15% on dedicated, token-level perplexity rose slightly on our eval set but pass-rate on the regen prompt set stayed within your acceptance threshold we discussed. we noted some minor hallucination patterns on very long context examples, flagged in the spreadsheet.
[02:12] Michael: hmm ok, that is expected tradeoff. cost delta?
[02:15] Jordan: rough numbers in the sheet - hosted per-token cost marginally higher than baseline on the standard model, but when you factor batching + KV cache + quantization recommendations the unit cost on dedicated drops ~20% vs baseline for this workload. we'll send a line-item estimate.
[02:31] Tom: latency tail still matters for us, our SLO is p95 < 300ms for user-facing requests. looks like dedicated hits that comfortably but hosted is borderline on p95 for some prompts.
[02:39] Priya: yep dedicated is the strong option for consistent tail; hosted can get there with our tuned batch policy and preferential routing, but if you need SLA-backed latency, Dedicated + reserved capacity is recommended.
[02:50] Michael: what about region/residency? our users are EU-first.
[02:53] Jordan: we can provision dedicated nodes in eu-west with private networking; also our private deployment option would let you run inside your VPC if compliance requires it. we'll include region pricing in the estimate.
[03:05] Sara: any regressions on function calling or structured outputs in quantized runs?
[03:09] Priya: function calling had negligible impact in most runs; structured JSON completions were within tolerance, we included sample outputs in the sheet. where we saw variance was very long chained tool-calls which hit p99 differently, noted as an action item to dig into.
[03:24] Jordan: ok let's go through the open questions from last week - 1) longer tail tests, 2) demo of dedicated routing, 3) security docs.
[03:31] Priya: on longer tail tests we scheduled a 10k-run overnight job last night, initial look shows p99 for Redwood dedicated at ~520ms vs baseline ~900ms, but we want to sanity-check anomalies.
[03:43] Michael: anomalies like spikes? can you share the trace samples?
[03:46] Priya: yes we'll dump a handful of trace ids and the raw logs to the spreadsheet.
[03:51] Tom: about routing, can Redwood route by latency SLO? like prefer dedicated when predicted latency > X?
[03:56] Jordan: yes we have smart routing policies - route by latency forecast, cost tiering, region. you can set a policy to fall back to cheaper variants unless predicted latency would breach SLO then serve from dedicated.
[04:10] Sara: security: we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for keys. do you have those docs?
[04:16] Jordan: yes SOC2 in the whitepaper link, SSO/SAML supported, RBAC, audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations documented. we'll attach the link right after the call.
[04:23] Michael: ok good. next steps from our side - we'll get you samples for the long tail prompts and the p95 SLO traffic pattern.
[04:29] Jordan: and we'll run the focused 10k run on quantized + non-quantized with the new batching config Priya recommended, and share raw logs and trace ids.
[04:36] Priya: action notes - i'll run the 1k quantized run per model variant and the 10k overnight, share sheet by tomorrow. also i'll add a small chart comparing tail latencies across variants.
[04:48] Michael: sounds good. any blockers?
[04:50] Tom: none from platform side, just want to validate network egress for dedicated nodes in eu-west, will confirm firewall rules.
[04:57] Jordan: great, we will follow up with the tuning session invite. thanks everyone.
[05:02] Michael: thanks all.
